title: Ankle-brachial index (ABI)
what: A nurse measures blood pressure on your arms and ankles. If it is much lower in the legs, the leg arteries may be narrowed.
why: For leg pain when walking, in smokers, with diabetes or high blood pressure, or to check the leg arteries.
duration: usually 15 to 20 minutes; results usually right away
tell_doctor: Leg pain when walking that goes away with rest
Wounds on your legs that heal poorly
If blood pressure cannot be taken on one of your arms

prepare.title: Rest
prepare.text: Come early and rest for 5 to 10 minutes. Do not smoke or drink coffee before the test.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Loose trousers or a skirt, so your ankles are easy to uncover. Socks that come off easily.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: No prep needed. You can eat.

steps: You lie on your back for a few minutes
Cuffs are put on both arms and both ankles
A small probe listens to the pulse on your arm and foot
The cuff is inflated and slowly let down
Blood pressure is measured at all four points
The device or the nurse calculates the index
feel: The cuff squeezes your arm and leg for a few seconds
after: You can go back to your usual day right away
If the index is abnormal, your doctor may order a leg artery ultrasound

faq.q: Why measure blood pressure on the legs?
faq.a: If the leg arteries are narrowed, the pressure there is lower than in the arms. It is a simple way to find a problem.
No. It is like a regular blood pressure check.

reminders.text: Ankle-brachial index test tomorrow. No smoking or coffee in the morning. Wear clothes you can easily pull up to the knees.
